text:
anya: RFC — adding variant-level quotas + guard checks to Experiment creation flow in Console. Quick sketch + questions. TL;DR: let variants declare guards that the routing proxy evaluates; if a guard fails, traffic falls back to a specified variant (or control).

anya: example config (rough):
```json
{
  "experiment_id": "exp.search.rank.2026-03",
  "variants": [
    {
      "id": "control",
      "weight": 90,
      "model": "redwood/base-1"
    },
    {
      "id": "v1-beta",
      "weight": 10,
      "model": "redwood/ensemble-v1",
      "quota_per_min": 200,
      "guards": [
        {"metric": "error_rate", "op": "<", "value": 0.005},
        {"metric": "latency_p95_ms", "op": "<", "value": 250}
      ],
      "fallback": "control"
    }
  ]
}
```

sam: prefer having guard evaluation in the routing layer (serving runtime) not the experiment manager. Fast path decision needs to be local and cheap.

mike: agree. also: we must emit per-variant telemetry (experiment_id + variant_id tags) so we can compute guard metrics in realtime. p95/err-rate at 1m/5m windows.

lina: UX idea: in Console show an "effective traffic" preview after estimated guard fail rate (based on historical telemetry or a conservative default). slider for rollout slope + a note about quotas. small tooltip: "Effective traffic = weight * (1 - estimated_guard_fail_rate)".

sam: question: quotas — are these enforced at gateway or advisory? e.g., quota_per_min=200 across hosted vs dedicated nodes. we need consistent semantics.

anya: proposal: two-level quota: "quota_per_min" (variant-level soft limit) + "enforce": {"hard": true|false}. routing layer enforces hard limits; platform checks aggregate against customer reserved capacity and warns in Console if overcommit.

mike: +1. Also add "rollout_schedule": {"duration_minutes": 30, "start_weight": 1, "end_weight": 10} so runtime can ramp. guards evaluated continuously during ramp.

lina: UX: provide presets ("canary", "quick-smoke", "percent-split") that populate sensible guard thresholds (err<0.5%, p95<250ms) and quota defaults.

anya: API debate: should guards be declarative metrics (error_rate, latency) or allow arbitrary metric expressions? declarative is easier for routing runtime but less flexible. Thoughts?

sam: start with declarative + an escape hatch of "external_check" that calls a low-latency policy service for complex logic. avoid putting heavy evals in hot path.

mike: don't forget quality metrics (semantic/regression) — add optional "quality_metric" guard (evaluated by async monitor) that can trigger automatic rollback but not per-request routing.

lina: small nit: Console should prevent conflicting settings like weight=0 + quota>0, or two variants claiming the same hard quota. validation error.

anya: great feedback. I'll draft an API PR + Console mockups. Sync to review API & runtime contract Thursday 9am PT? @sam @mike @lina :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: anya created draft PR #4321 (links) and attached a Console mock PNG.

sam: :+1: see you Thu.

mike: :ok_hand: Thanks, this covers the main edges.

lina: love the presets idea, will mock them up before Thurs.

anya: thanks all — will post the PR link here when ready.
